question: Should `crawlkit` intentionally stop publishing Developer ID-signed `crawlctl` artifacts and replace the current GitHub-release contract with source-only `go install` distribution?
rationale: The branch changes a documented release and binary-trust contract rather than making a narrow implementation repair; current repository policy requires a retained signed-artifact route for GitHub releases.

options.title: Preserve signed artifacts
options.body: Keep the signed-tag Go module flow, but retain the repository release scripts, workflow, and macOS artifacts required by the current policy.

options.title: Approve source-only releases
options.body: Explicitly revise the repository release policy and approve a supported migration and verification plan before removing the existing signed artifact path.

recommendation.title: Preserve signed artifacts
recommendation.body: Keep the signed-tag Go module flow, but retain the repository release scripts, workflow, and macOS artifacts required by the current policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR directly proposes the release-model change and identifies the rationale and affected signing workflow.
